a2302ae2a8.q: How does divorce affect FERS pension benefits and survivor annuity for federal employees?
a2302ae2a8.a: Federal employees can negotiate with their spouse on how to split pension benefits through their divorce decree, which OPM will follow exactly. Survivor annuity requires either a 10% pension reduction to leave 50% to the ex-spouse, or a 5% reduction to leave 25%. The key constraint is that if you remarry, there is a 50% cap on total pension benefits you can leave behind across all beneficiaries combined.

93de889ec1.q: What happens to TSP accounts in a federal employee divorce settlement?
93de889ec1.a: TSP splits are negotiated between spouses and TSP will pay the ex-spouse directly without requiring the employee to take a taxable withdrawal first. This direct payment structure means the money going to the ex-spouse does not create a taxable event for the employee.

0823f270ee.q: Can federal employees keep FEHB health insurance for ex-spouses after divorce?
0823f270ee.a: FEHB can be negotiated for ex-spouses but it is not as straightforward as other benefits. If an ex-spouse remarries before age 55, they lose FEHB coverage, and they normally have to pay higher premiums. The structure depends on how important this benefit is and what both parties negotiate.

5d9cada097.q: Do federal employee beneficiary designations automatically update after a divorce?
5d9cada097.a: Divorce does not automatically update beneficiary designations. If an ex-spouse is still listed as a beneficiary on life insurance, IRAs, TSP, 401ks, or other assets, those benefits will go to them upon death even after divorce. Federal employees must manually update all beneficiary designations themselves.

5fb5117be5.q: Is there a better time to divorce as a federal employee relative to retirement timing?
5fb5117be5.a: Timing divorce before retirement provides more options than timing it after retirement, such as electing survivor benefits and making adjustments to federal benefits. After retirement, there are fewer options to adjust benefit elections.
